usageNotes: Use this to define a new network interface (bridge, bond, VLAN, OVS type, etc.) in the node's /etc/network/interfaces — the config is written to disk but does NOT take effect until you apply pending changes via PUT /nodes/{node}/network. The caller must hold Sys.Modify on /nodes/{node}. Only one of cidr/address+netmask is needed for IPv4; gateway should only be set on the interface that carries the default route.

examples.summary: Create a VLAN-aware Linux bridge vmbr1 with a static IP on node pve1

params.comments: VM guest traffic bridge - VLAN trunk

tips: Changes are staged only — always follow up with PUT /nodes/{node}/network (apply) or the node network will remain unchanged until the next reboot or manual ifup.
For a plain bond, set type=bond and list member interfaces in 'slaves'; for OVS bonds use ovs_bonds instead.
Setting gateway on more than one interface will produce a broken routing table — only set it on the primary uplink interface.
bridge_vids is only evaluated when bridge_vlan_aware is true; omit it to allow all VLANs.
Interface names must be 2–20 characters and follow Linux iface naming rules (no spaces, no slashes).
